shower.thought: We spend the first half of our lives learning to do things and the second half learning we didn't need to do most of them.
If you can imagine it, someone has probably already felt awkward about it.
The older you get, the more you realize that "good advice" is just someone else's regret wearing a disguise.
You can't actually remember most of your life, so you're essentially living with a stranger who has all your passwords.
Silence isn't the absence of sound—it's the absence of anything demanding your attention.
The reason we're nostalgic for our childhoods isn't that they were better; it's that we had fewer options to regret.
You never truly fail at something until you stop trying, which means most of us are still technically in the middle of everything we've ever quit.
Every conversation ends, but you only remember the ones where you think of the perfect thing to say three days later.
The scariest part of growing up isn't becoming your parents—it's realizing they were just as confused as you are now.
Your body keeps score of every embarrassing moment, but your memory is merciful enough to make most of them blurry.
We call it "networking" when we're desperate and "friendship" when it works out.
The moment you stop caring what people think is the exact moment you start becoming interesting to them.
You can't actually know if you're happy right now because you'll judge it against your future unhappiness.
Everyone's a little bit crazy; the well-adjusted people just have better documentation practices.
Time moves slower when you're waiting for something and faster when you're dreading it, which means time is just a story your anxiety tells.
The things that scare you most about the future are usually things that would've seemed normal to you five years ago.
You learn more about people from how they treat someone who can't help them than from how they treat someone who can.
We're all just trying to build a life stable enough that we can afford to think about deeper things.
Confidence isn't knowing you're right—it's being okay with finding out you're wrong.
The people you miss most are often the ones you took for granted while they were still around.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she'd be prettier if she smiled more.
Turns out she was smiling—I just couldn't see her face through the tears.

My therapist asked if I ever feel like people don't listen to me.
I said, "I don't think so," and she just nodded and checked her phone.

I'm at that age where my back goes out more than I do.
Last week my spine threw its own going-away party.

My dad said, "Son, I'm not angry, just disappointed."
I said, "Why not both?" and he left. Still works.

I joined a gym to get healthier.
So far I've mostly just paid $50 a month to feel guilty.

My neighbor asked if I wanted to join his suicide prevention group.
I said, "What's the catch?"

People say money can't buy happiness.
They've clearly never experienced the joy of being alone with the lights off at 2 AM.

I tried to make a joke about my depression to lighten the mood.
Nobody laughed. My therapist said that's progress.

My dating profile says I'm "brutally honest."
Turns out "brutally" is doing a lot of heavy lifting there.

I asked my mom why she never talks about my childhood.
She said, "We try not to."

My wife asked if I think she's put on weight.
I said, "No, I think I've gotten used to disappointment."

I told my doctor about my anxiety.
He said, "Have you tried not worrying?"
I said, "Have you tried not being useless?"

My friend said he's going through an existential crisis.
I said, "At least something's going through something."

I love the smell of coffee in the morning.
It's the only thing that makes me want to be awake.

My boss asked what my five-year plan is.
I said, "Honestly, I'm just trying to make it to lunch."

People keep asking if I want kids.
I say, "I barely want myself."

I told my therapist I have trust issues.
She said, "You can trust me," and I said, "See, that's where you're wrong."

My dentist said I need to floss more.
I said, "You know what else I should do more? Live."

I failed my driving test three times.
The examiner said I was too reckless. I said, "That's quitter talk."

I went to a self-help seminar about overcoming pessimism.
Worst $200 I ever spent.
